why: Repositories waiting on a first judging pass. [CORPUS-REGISTER-COVERAGE] A repository cannot become a register until a judge has ruled on its pairs, and a judge cannot rule on pairs until a comparison has produced two reports for it — so a repository that is not yet judged still has to be scanned. This file is that queue: the comparison scans every register plus everything here, and `make judging-folder` turns each into a workspace. When the verdicts come back, the repository moves into corpus/register/ and out of this list. Every entry is pinned to a full commit id for the same reason a register is: the judge and the scan must read identical source.

repositories.name: ripgrep
repositories.why: No Rust has ever been judged. A search tool with several small crates in one workspace, so the same helper is genuinely written more than once.

repositories.name: zod
repositories.why: No TypeScript has ever been judged. Dense generic types and one schema class per primitive, which is exactly the shape that makes a boilerplate call hard.

repositories.name: guzzle
repositories.why: No PHP has ever been judged. Small enough to compare quickly, and its handler stack repeats a middleware shape that should test the precision side.

repositories.name: bloc
repositories.why: No Dart has ever been judged. A multi-package repository where sibling packages deliberately mirror each other's API, so both verdicts should be reachable.

repositories.name: FSharp.Data
repositories.why: No F# has ever been judged. Type providers repeat a large amount of near-identical shape, which is the hardest case for a duplicate detector to call correctly.
